qc.label_under_test: A second, mirrored labelling clause that casts the speaker or the listener: after one clause casts someone as something (sees him as a hero, calls her a liar), a following clause casts me, us or you (and she sees me as a nuisance, they treat us as outsiders, and he calls you a snob); it fires on the 'as' or 'a' right after 'me'/'us'/'you'. 'You' fires when you did the first labelling (you treat them as family, and they treat you as staff); after 'I see him as...', a second clause casting you stays weak. The same second clause aimed at him, her or them is weak, as is a one-way label of me or you with no earlier labelling clause, or me labelled in the first clause and answering back. Strongest when a sentence of setting comes first.

fire: The office was quiet that Monday. My boss sees Daniel as a genius, and she sees me as a nuisance.
We moved to the village last spring. The locals treat the old baker as a legend, but they treat us as outsiders.
The dinner party ran late. Everyone called Marco a charmer, and then they called me a bore.
It was the first week of term. The teacher regards Priya as a natural leader, while she regards me as a troublemaker.
The tournament ended in chaos. The fans hailed the striker as a hero and branded us as cheats.
You've worked at the café for years. You treat the regulars as family, and they treat you as staff.
The family reunion was tense again. Grandma thinks of my cousin as a saint, and she thinks of me as a lost cause.
Rain kept everyone indoors. The kids called the new boy a show-off, and later they called us a pair of snobs.
